claims.text: Annealing HfZrTiTa0.53 for 0.5–2 hours just below its recrystallization threshold followed by rapid quenching will induce controlled nanoscale precipitation.
The heat treatment will produce a bimodal microstructure containing an ultrafine-grained matrix and evenly distributed nanoscale precipitates.
The nanoscale precipitates in the treated alloy will constitute a ductile secondary phase.
The ultrafine-grained matrix will preserve the alloy's high yield and compressive strengths.
Nanoscale precipitates will improve tensile ductility and uniform elongation.
As-fabricated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-fabricated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
As-fabricated HfZrTiTa0.53 has approximately 13.5% terminal tensile strain or tensile strain at failure.
The applicable improvement regime is room-temperature quasi-static tensile loading at approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The precipitates will blunt crack initiation and propagation.
The precipitates will provide additional sites for dislocation accumulation.
Crack blunting and additional dislocation accumulation will delay localized necking.
The treatment will increase elongation by at least 50%, from approximately 13.5% to more than 20%.
After treatment, yield strength will remain within 10% of the as-fabricated value.
After treatment, compressive strength will be maintained.
Untreated TiZrHfTa0.53 exhibits pronounced energy release and combustion during high-velocity penetration into steel.
The heat-treated alloy will maintain the impact-triggered energy-release performance of untreated HfZrTiTa0.53.
Changes in annealing time, annealing temperature, or quenching rate that alter precipitate size or distribution could eliminate the strength or ductility gains.
Matched as-fabricated and heat-treated specimens will be compared using room-temperature tension, compression, and high-strain-rate impact tests.
Failure to exceed 20% elongation while retaining yield strength within 10%, or measurable degradation in compression or impact performance, is intended to falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats terminal strain or strain at failure and uniform elongation as interchangeable. Uniform elongation ends at necking, whereas terminal strain at failure can include post-necking deformation, so the 13.5% baseline and >20% target are not consistently defined.
